summary: Intermittent 429s for enterprise customer after enabling ingress smoothing flag in hybrid dedicated+hosted traffic
description:
Issue summary:
Customer AtlasRetail reported intermittent 429 (Too Many Requests) errors beginning 2026-03-11 after Support enabled the experimental 'ingress_smoothing_on' feature for their hybrid deployment (Dedicated pool + Hosted routing). Errors are seen primarily on low-throughput API keys used by background workers and on real-time checkout validation flows.

Impact:
- Several checkout validation calls (latency-sensitive) returned 429s, causing retry storms in the customer's worker pool.
- The error rate for affected keys spiked to ~15% for short periods (1-5 minutes) during normal traffic.
- Customer visible impact: order delays and retries; customer has flagged this as P1.

Environment:
- Customer: AtlasRetail Inc., enterprise tier, dedicated GPU pool (dedicated-01) in us-east-1 with hosted fallback in eu-west-1.
- API: /v1/chat/completions and /v1/embeddings.
- Flag toggled: ingress_smoothing_on = true (applied 2026-03-11 22:13 UTC).
- Observed across both model variants listed above.

Steps to reproduce (as documented by customer):
1) Send intermittent low-volume background requests (1-4 rps per API key) to /v1/embeddings from us-east-1 agent pool.
2) Send real-time checkout requests (burst to 6 rps sustained for 10s) to /v1/chat/completions.
3) Observe ~5-20% of responses return HTTP 429 during brief windows.

Observed behavior:
- 429 responses include RateLimit-Remaining headers showing 0 tokens left for the tenant during the spike window.
- Console shows token windows refilling, but token bucket counters on the edge were inconsistent with origin counters.
- Dedicated pool autoscaler did not show scale activity in the same minute as spikes.

Expected behavior:
- Smoothing should reduce microbursts without causing under-refill or double-accounting across edge and origin, and low-throughput keys should not be penalized by smoothing across pooled traffic.

Logs / Evidence:
- Customer provided sample request IDs: req_us_4982ae, req_eu_b8c91f (attached).
- Dashboard links: https://console.redwood.ai/customers/atlasretail/rate-heatmap?start=2026-03-11T22:00Z&end=2026-03-12T02:00Z
- Support trace: https://console.redwood.ai/traces/trace-9a7f0

Initial hypothesis:
- The ingress smoothing algorithm applies a tenant-level refill smoothing at the edge that can interact with dedicated pool route-weighting and cause temporary under-allocation for low-throughput API keys when hybrid routing is active.
- Another contributor: time skew between edge proxies in us-east and origin refill ledger leading to a brief period where edge believes tenant credits are exhausted while origin shows available credits.

Requested by customer:
- Temporary disable smoothing for their tenant or reduce smoothing aggressiveness until a stable fix is in place.
- Explanation of root cause and confirmation that billing/credits are not consumed incorrectly.
comments: 2026-03-12 09:24 - Support (Maya Chen): Logged initial ticket after customer submitted console traces and request IDs. Customer asked for an immediate mitigation; suggested toggling ingress_smoothing flag off as a quick rollback.

2026-03-12 10:01 - SRE (Liam O'Connor): Correlated spike windows with the moment the flag was toggled. Found edge-origin refill offset around ~3s in a subset of us-east edge nodes. Opening investigation to check token ledger propagation.

2026-03-12 11:40 - Eng (Priya Nair): Ran a replay of low-volume keys against staging with smoothing enabled. Reproduced 429s when route-weight favors hosted fallback during probe windows. Suspect double-throttling: edge smoothing + route-weight enforcement.

2026-03-12 14:05 - Support (Maya Chen): Escalated to customer with two mitigations: (1) disable ingress_smoothing for their tenant (2) temporarily increase per-route burst pool for checkout route. Customer chose to disable smoothing first.
2026-03-12 16:22 - Customer (AtlasRetail - Devops) via email: Confirmed disabling smoothing reduced 429s within 4 minutes. Asking for permanent fix and audit that no extra billing occurred.

2026-03-13 08:18 - Billing (Anika Patel): Verified billing increments for the tenant during the spike windows; tokens were consumed normally and no billing anomaly observed. Sent audit snapshot to Support.

2026-03-13 12:10 - Eng (Priya Nair): Drafted patch to ensure edge refill checks a short-lived origin token snapshot before returning 429s for low-throughput keys. Opened PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rate-limiter/pull/221

2026-03-14 07:44 - SRE (Liam O'Connor): Deployed temporary hotfix to edge nodes in us-east to align refill timestamps; monitoring for recurrence. Initial metrics show 429 rate down to <0.5% for affected keys.
2026-03-14 12:00 - Support (Maya Chen): Notified customer of temporary hotfix and proposed timeline for full patch (PR review + canary) over next 72 hours. Customer accepted canary plan.
investigation_notes: Edge-Origin refill drift measured: 2.8s median, 6s p95 on us-east edges during 2026-03-11 22:10-22:20 UTC window.
Reproduction in staging requires both: enabling ingress_smoothing and a mixed route weight where hosted fallback receives >20% of requests intermittently.
Token bucket logic: smoothing reduces refill amplitude; when combined with route-weight route-level clamp, low-volume keys can see transient 0 remaining leading to 429s.
Audit: billing confirms token consumption consistent with the returned 429s (no negative billing).
resolution_notes: Workaround applied (2026-03-12): ingress_smoothing toggled off for AtlasRetail tenant. Customer confirmed immediate improvement.
Hotfix deployed to align edge refill clock with origin ledger on us-east edges (2026-03-14). Reduced median drift to <200ms.
Code patch PR #221 created to add origin snapshot grace-period check before final 429 is emitted for low-throughput keys. Planned canary rollout across us-east on 2026-03-15.

Follow-ups: (1) add automated test for smoothing+route-weight interaction, (2) update runbook to include 'disable smoothing' rollback step, (3) product decision on default smoothing behavior for hybrid deployments. Assigned to Priya Nair (eng) and SRE team.
next_steps: 2026-03-15 - Canary rollout of PR #221 in us-east (Liam O'Connor)
2026-03-15 - Run integration test that simulates low-throughput keys with mixed route-weight (Priya Nair)
2026-03-16 - Postmortem draft and runbook update (Support + SRE)
Confirm with customer after canary: keep smoothing disabled until full rollout is validated or re-enable with adjusted parameters.
